title: Progressive tooltip prefetch and delta-sampling for time-series charts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Time-series tooltips (especially on high-cardinality charts) are a major source of UI jank and backend token/CPU usage due to full-series aggregation on hover and synchronous hit-testing. Goal: introduce a progressive tooltip strategy that reduces CPU and data loading by prefetching a narrow 'prefetch-window' and using delta-sampling + quadrant-based hit-test hints to provide immediate, accessible summaries while progressively resolving details.
background: Current behavior: on hover we run full-series aggregation to populate tooltip rows, compute annotations, and fetch enrichment (anomaly tags, linked logs). With dense series and long time windows this causes 100-300ms stalls and higher backend cost for every hover move. Past tickets focused on legend condensation and ARIA announcers; this ticket targets tooltip workflows and the interaction layer between chart runtime and data router.
proposal: Design system changes: (1) Introduce a UI pattern 'Progressive Tooltip' with three phases: summary (0-40ms) - minimal content from precomputed sampling; detail (40-200ms) - incremental rows populated via background fetch; enrich (200+ms) - optional enrichments (anomaly badges, log-links) fetched lazily. (2) Define a delta-sampling algorithm: sample N points around mouse x-position (prefetch-window) and compute an 'aggregate fingerprint' rather than full-fold aggregation. (3) Add hit-test-quadrant-hinting: chart runtime returns a small hint of top 3 series ids per quadrant to avoid scanning all series on main thread. (4) ARIA: provide concise aria-live summary for the summary phase and make detail rows focusable when ready.
tradeoffs: - Pros: significantly lower perceived latency, lower CPU spikes, predictable backend load. - Cons: slightly more complexity in runtime (hinting APIs), risk of perceived flicker as rows populate, may need guardrails for critical exact-value flows (financial apps). - Accessibility: summary must be sufficient; edge cases where detail never loads (network) must degrade gracefully.
tasks: Design token: define new tooltip micro-variant (progressive) in tokens file with condensed spacing and visual placeholder state
Design: craft Figma prototype showing three-phase tooltip states and keyboard/voiced navigation flows
Engineering (runtime): implement hit-test-quadrant-hinting protocol and sampling API contract
Engineering (data): add prefetch-window endpoint to router that returns sampled aggregates and top-k ids
QA: build synthetic load tests with 500+ series and measure p95 hover latency before/after
Accessibility: write aria-live copy for summary and keyboard focus behavior; run with accessibility engineer
Docs: update design system tooltip doc and migration notes for components using full-value tooltips
acceptance_criteria: Tooltips render summary content within 50ms on p95 under test workload (500 series, 10s window)
Detail rows populate progressively without blocking main thread; no layout shift > 8px when rows arrive
Keyboard users can reach tooltip content and receive the aria-live summary upon focus; screen reader testing passes with VoiceOver and NVDA
Backend requests per hover reduced by >= 70% in sampling mode compared to full aggregation
Design tokens and Figma prototype merged and linked; migration guide exists
